verdict.oneLineSummary: The gold standard baseline: 10 minutes setup, 0 days wait, immediate public access.

twoClocks.anyUserCanConnect: Same day — no provider review required

capabilityCheck.question: Can an agent read AND write on the user's behalf?
capabilityCheck.detail: OAuth scopes grant read and write to repositories, issues, pull requests, and gists per the scopes requested. No capability ceiling for standard agent workflows.

prerequisites: A GitHub personal or organization account

steps.text: Go to Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New OAuth App. (Avoid 'GitHub Apps' if you only want basic user auth).

fields.name: Authorization callback URL
fields.note: Must match your redirect URI exactly

fields.name: Enable Device Flow
fields.note: Unchecked unless building a headless CLI / terminal tool

steps.text: Register the application, copy the Client ID, and click 'Generate a new client secret'.
steps.note: Save the client secret immediately; it will never be displayed again.

steps.text: Request scopes dynamically at connect time inside your application authorization URL.
steps.note: Unlike Google or Slack, GitHub OAuth Apps do not pre-register scopes in the console; scopes are requested dynamically in the OAuth URL query parameter.

scopes.note: Full read/write access to code, issues, and PRs (instant, no review)

blockers.issue: Developers frequently click 'New GitHub App' instead of 'New OAuth App'. GitHub Apps enforce a required Webhook URL if the 'Active' checkbox is checked.
blockers.workaround: Choose 'OAuth Apps' for simple user connections. If using GitHub Apps, uncheck Webhook → Active.

composio.recommendation: Composio provides instant managed GitHub connections out of the box with zero OAuth app registration needed.

evidence.claim: Registered a GitHub OAuth app end-to-end in ~10 minutes with no provider review; any public user can authorize immediately.
evidence.label: TESTED
